notes.key_messages: Read the questions carefully and answer the question asked. Candidates should know the difference between command words e.g. state, describe, explain, calculate and suggest and the expected response for each command word.
notes.general_comments: Candidates were prepared well for the examination. The marks covered the whole range of abilities. It is essential that candidates read questions carefully and make sure they are following all the instructions given. As many candidates showed a good knowledge and understanding of the topic, but the question asked was not answered. It should also be emphasised that marks are never awarded for simply restating the question. The paper asked for a number of definitions for words and processes. Candidates should learn these definitions and have an understanding of what they mean. Most candidates were able to complete all sections and there was no indication that the time allowed was insufficient.
notes.1a: Few candidates could state a feature common to all arthropods. Many gave feature particular to one arthropod group such as antennae or six legs.
notes.1bi: Insects was a common correct answer. A common incorrect answer was myriapods.
notes.1bii: The features chosen must be visible in Fig. 1.1. This was not appreciated by some candidates. Antennae and wings were common correct responses.
notes.2ai: Very few candidates read the words ‘in structure’ and consequently many gave incorrect answers that referred to the type of blood and which way the blood was travelling.
notes.2aii: Blood in vessel D is low pressure and oxygenated. The most frequent wrong answer was high pressure, oxygenated.
notes.2aiii: All four boxes had to be correct to score the three marks. Most candidates were able to select one correct box but few could select all four.
notes.3ai: A correct answer of transpiration or evaporation was given by most candidates.
notes.3aii: This question proved challenging for many and while all candidates were able to select one correct box few managed to correctly sequence all four. There was no consistent pattern to the wrong responses given.
notes.3bi: Candidates were asked to use the data in Fig. 3.2 to answer this question about how the volume of water in jar H had changed and suggest an explanation for the change. They were not asked about any other jar or for a comparison with other jars. Therefore responses about the number of leaves and size of flower did not answer the question. The description should have been about the shape of the graph and the explanation is that water is absorbed because it is used by the plant or lost so needs replacing. There was also credit for data usage.
notes.3bii: This was a simple calculation using figures extracted from the graph of G and H at midday but surprisingly few got the correct answer of 45.
notes.3biii: Many candidates were able to answer this question correctly.
notes.4a: This was the first definition on the paper. Many candidates found this challenging and could not define what a balanced diet is. While some knew what a ‘diet’ was they were unable to further qualify their responses sufficiently to state what a balance diet was.
notes.4bi: Many candidates realised that the foods listed were rich in carbohydrates and that they were needed for energy.
notes.4bii: At least two foods high in protein should have been named and many candidates wrote all six categories. Some also went on to say that they were needed for growth or repair of cells or named body parts. A common misconception was that they were needed for energy.
notes.4biii: Diabetes, obesity and heart problems were popular correct answers (iv) This question was misinterpreted by some candidates. The factors affecting a person’s dietary needs are age, gender, activity, pregnancy and others. Two of these should have been stated and then an explanation offered as to how this factor affected the person’s needs.
notes.5a: Many candidates did not write a definition but instead gave examples of the uses of genetic engineering instead.
notes.5bi: Some candidates were able to recall the definition of a gene but many gave responses that discussed traits or characteristics being passed from one generation to another rather than a length of DNA that codes for a protein.
notes.5bii: A few candidates were able to correctly identify that the maize would kill insects which would lead to a higher crop yield.
notes.5ci: A few candidates were able to correctly describe pollination.
notes.5cii: The idea of fewer pollinators/insects was realised by many candidates. Alternatively they wrote about the trees not being pollinated.
notes.5d: Some candidates gave good examples of genetic engineering. A common error was to give a description of selective breeding or how to create new genes.
notes.6a: A few candidates were able to give a correct definition. Some knew it was a chemical and some knew it was carried in the blood. Most wrote about the effects of hormones especially the sex hormones.
notes.6bi: Most candidates were able to identify the reproductive organs and state corresponding hormones. Fewer could identify the adrenal glands, pancreas and their associated hormones.
notes.6bii: The majority of candidates understood the stimuli that trigger the release of adrenaline and proved correct responses to this question.
notes.7a: Some candidate responses gave ‘uses’ rather referring to why bacteria are ‘useful’ and this did not answer the question. A few candidates were able to identify valid reasons such as a fast reproductive rate and the ability to make complex molecules.
notes.7bi: Some candidates were able to provide the correct response many found this question challenging.
notes.7bii: Candidates knew that above 60°C the enzymes do not function and many knew the term denatured. They did not fully answer the question by explaining why the recommended temperature is 30°C.
notes.7c: Very few candidates correctly answered lipase. Most wrote amylase.
notes.8ai: (ii) The position and the names of parts of the eye were not known by most candidates.
notes.8bi: Inherited is the transmission of genetic information from generation to generation. Few candidates were able to state what was passed from generation to generation in sufficient detail. Common responses discussed passing of traits and characteristics but made no reference to genetic information.
notes.8bii: The terms recessive and allele were known to only a few candidates.
notes.8c: Some candidates did very well in this question. The key was to realise that those who suffer from glaucoma must be gg (double recessive), then in order for there to be non-sufferers the others must be heterozygous (Gg).
notes.9ai: Nearly all candidates gave a good definition of the term herbivore.
notes.9aii: Many candidates could name the organisms that break down dead or decaying matter as decomposers.
notes.9aiii: Most candidates copied out the statements from Fig. 9.1 which was insufficient. The ideas that nutrients and water are recycled and it is a self-contained system were some of the reasons expected.
notes.9b: Many candidates were uncertain of the differences between sustainable and renewable.
notes.10a: Many candidates knew that the amniotic fluid was for protection.
notes.10b: Many candidates sequenced all the stages correctly.
